# Agent Factory Lab — Full Content for LLMs

> Open research lab testing techniques to make AI coding agents faster, cheaper, and more reliable.
> All numbers below are from actual experiment runs. Each is labeled as real, estimated, or simulated.

## About

Agent Factory Lab is a hands-on research repository for improving two AI coding agents:
- Gwaihir: orchestrator for herdr, a multi-agent coding tool
- Landroval: orchestrator for Rex, a coding factory

Findings are collected from X (Twitter), documented with source links, and each has a runnable experiment. The repo includes a sample codebase with 10 seeded Python bugs and a test suite for benchmarking.

## Finding 1: Cross-Model Writer/Reviewer/QA Pipeline

Source: https://x.com/brag_sheet/status/2117474234431869338

Use a multi-agent pipeline where distinct models fill separate roles (writer, reviewer, QA), each in an isolated git worktree. A deterministic risk gate scores changes by lines changed, files touched, and blast radius before deciding to auto-merge or escalate.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — Monte Carlo, 1000 trials × 10 bugs):
- Single-agent fix rate: 64.2%
- Pipeline fix rate: 79.2% (+15 percentage points)
- Defect escapes reduced: 42%
- Token cost increase: 71%
- Average review rounds: 1.28

Proposal: Make this Gwaihir's default pipeline. Harness ready for real LLM calls.

## Finding 2: Keep Frontier Models Off the Control Plane

Source: https://x.com/adamhjk/status/2116417623789613265

Route orchestration (status checks, routing, task decomposition) to cheap/fast models. Reserve frontier models for code generation and complex reasoning.

Experiment result (ESTIMATED — real API prices, synthetic 17-step session):
- All-frontier cost: $1.3808 per session
- Two-tier cost: $1.0924 per session
- Savings: $0.2884 (20.9%)
- Control-plane token share: 28% of input

Using Claude Opus ($15/M input) vs Claude Haiku ($0.25/M input). Sessions with more orchestration could save 50%+.

## Finding 3: Programmatic / Batched Tool Calling

Source: https://x.com/MilanGlow/status/2116089358709370962

Batch many tool calls into a single script instead of issuing them one at a time. Eliminates repeated context window overhead.

Experiment result (REAL — tiktoken cl100k_base token counting):
- Per-call: 20 requests, 32,981 total tokens
- Batched: 2 requests, 1,819 total tokens
- Token reduction: 94.5%
- Request reduction: 90%

The per-call approach causes quadratic token growth (74 tokens at request 1 → 2,151 at request 20) from re-sending conversation history. Batching eliminates this.

## Finding 4: Server-Side Prompt Caching

Sources: https://x.com/ClaudeDevs/status/2117332449382510884, https://x.com/tokenscost/status/2117638485075206393

Cache the stable prefix (system prompt, tools, early context) and charge cached tokens at a discount. Requires append-only conversation history.

Experiment result (REAL token counts, ESTIMATED costs — tiktoken + Anthropic pricing):
- Uncached session cost: $0.0274
- Cached session cost: $0.0076
- Savings: $0.0198 (72.3%)
- Cache hit rate: 92.7%
- Break-even turn: 2

20-turn session with $3/M input, $0.30/M cached, $3.75/M cache write.

## Finding 5: Native Pane/Tab Control & Durable Session Layer

Sources: https://x.com/dani_avila7/status/2116352019564777669, https://x.com/herdrdev/status/2115841099575222765, https://x.com/nicoritschel/status/2116931517415141724

Give agents programmatic control over terminal panes (edit, test, logs in parallel). Pair with durable session persistence for crash recovery.

Experiment result (REAL — tmux execution + JSON checkpoint):
- Sequential execution: 0.300s average
- Parallel execution: 0.164s average
- Speedup: 1.83x
- Session checkpoint/restore: zero state loss, 0.061s resume time

Pane manager is ~80 lines of Python. Session store is ~40 lines.

## Finding 6: SuperPlane Backlog-to-Ship Pattern

Source: https://x.com/darkofabijan/status/2115037955480048100

Automate the full lifecycle: issue triage → planning → approval → execution → review → merge → deploy.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — state machine with 5 sample issues):
- 4/5 issues auto-shipped through the pipeline
- 1/5 escalated to human (high-risk, no tests)
- Risk gates: low-risk auto-merges, medium-risk requires human merge, high-risk requires human approval

Landroval needs 10 capabilities for the full pattern: issue tracker integration, automatic triage, plan generation, approval gate, code generation, test execution, risk-gated merge, deploy trigger, metrics collection, escalation notifications.

## Recommendations

High-confidence (real measurements):
1. Adopt batched tool calling: 94.5% token savings
2. Enable prompt caching: 72% cost savings, break-even at turn 2
3. Add pane management: 1.83x speedup, trivial implementation

Medium-confidence (cost models):
4. Two-tier model routing: 21% savings, validate with A/B test
5. Writer/reviewer default pipeline: +15pp fix rate, calibrate with real LLMs

Longer-term (design-stage):
6. SuperPlane pattern for Landroval: state machine ready, 10-item checklist
7. herdr-core session persistence: prototype works, needs API integration

## Finding 7: Cap AI Review at 3 Rounds with Findings Log

Sources: https://x.com/i/status/2114604912520921136, https://x.com/Bic_Revelation/status/2115286181592346745

Cap review loops at 3 rounds. Maintain a findings.jsonl log the reviewer checks before commenting to avoid repeated notes. After round 3, re-plan from scratch.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — Monte Carlo, 1000 trials × 10 bugs):
- Uncapped avg rounds: 1.40, Capped avg rounds: 1.38
- Token reduction: 5.2% (target ≥30% not met with easy bugs; cap is more valuable for hard bugs)

## Finding 8: Bug Priority Gate (freq × severity ≥ 5)

Source: https://x.com/Voxyz_ai/status/2116575932957762004

Fix bugs only when frequency × severity ≥ 5. Otherwise file an issue. Never trust another agent's "done" without verification.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — 15-bug backlog):
- Bugs fixed: 12/15, Bugs filed: 3/15
- Token savings: 17.8%
- High-severity bugs missed: 0

## Finding 9: Score the Reviewer Against Past Incidents

Source: https://x.com/i/status/2114604912520921136

Evaluate reviewer effectiveness against historical data: past incidents, reverts, known-clean PRs.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — 20-PR corpus, 500 trials):
- Catch rate (recall): 75.7%
- False-alarm rate: 15.2%
- Precision: 83.3%, F1: 0.793

## Finding 10: Stop Hook — Block "Done" Until Checks Pass

Sources: https://x.com/Cozy2054934/status/2113838957901537487, https://x.com/Hotfixdaily/status/2112969533203869787

Gate the "done" signal on test/typecheck/build passing. Include command output as evidence.

Experiment result (REAL — pytest execution):
- Buggy code: 0 passed, 10 failed → hook BLOCKED
- Fixed code: 10 passed, 0 failed → hook PASSED
- Reopen rate: from 35% (estimated without hook) to 0% (with hook)

## Finding 11: Mutation Check

Source: https://x.com/ganesh2412/status/2115458572519968930

Make 3-5 deliberate breaks per changed function. Require at least one test to fail for each mutation.

Experiment result (REAL — code mutation + pytest):
- Mutations applied: 10
- Killed (test caught): 10
- Survived (test missed): 0
- Kill rate: 100%

## Finding 12: HANDOFF.md + Context-Window Restart

Sources: https://x.com/iskakovdev/status/2115803578145394794, https://x.com/AaronDelz/status/2115120640072323162

Write HANDOFF.md under 60 lines instead of full transcript. Restart context past 150K tokens or 60 min idle.

Experiment result (REAL — tiktoken token counting):
- Full transcript: 561 tokens
- HANDOFF.md: 263 tokens (53.1% reduction)
- Key facts retained: 13/13 (100%)
- Under 60 lines: Yes (35 lines)

## Finding 13: Two Corrections → Skill; Prune Unused

Source: https://x.com/educalvolpz/status/2115004827910496389

When the same correction appears twice, extract a reusable skill. Prune skills that never prevent corrections.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — 50 sessions, 150 corrections):
- Skills extracted: 10
- Skills pruned: 0
- All correction types seen ≥2 times were captured

## Finding 14: AGENTS.md as Single Source + CLAUDE.md Pointer

Sources: https://x.com/mariioalexandre/status/2116333676048892182, https://x.com/sachintwtss/status/2114947225780355191, https://x.com/triedthatai/status/2117255711537426839

One AGENTS.md as source of truth. CLAUDE.md says @AGENTS.md. Sub-agents use omitClaudeMd.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — 4 agents, 30 edits):
- Single source: 0 divergent copies, 0 drift
- Duplicated: 3 unique versions, 6.5 avg rule drift

## Finding 15: Stop Writing Once Verification Passes

Source: https://x.com/Best_Ethan_/status/2116070176395301057

Emit a 3-line report after verification passes. Lower reasoning effort on final turn.

Experiment result (REAL — tiktoken):
- Verbose: 415 tokens, Terse: 18 tokens
- Reduction: 95.7%
- Particle's claim: ~45% (our terse is more aggressive)

## Finding 16: Agent Races

Sources: https://x.com/stretchcloud/status/2115937472550965267, https://x.com/kinabalu/status/2117732717131391359

Run 2-3 models in parallel on hard tasks. Pick the winner. Majority vote for risky actions.

Experiment result (SIMULATED — 500 trials × 100 tasks):
- Single agent: 59.8% success
- Race 2: 81.7% success (2x cost)
- Race 3: 91.2% success (3x cost)
- Majority vote: 57.3% (safety layer)

## Finding 17 (Extra): Rex on Remote VM

Source: https://x.com/denCual/status/2115801768571621812

Run Rex on a remote Linux VM so sessions survive laptop sleeping.

Experiment result (REAL — tmux sessions):
- Survival rate: 100% (5/5 cycles)
- Avg reconnect time: 0.005s
- State loss: none

## How to Run

git clone https://github.com/andrebrov/agent-factory-lab.git
cd agent-factory-lab
pip install tiktoken pytest
bash run_all.sh

Each experiment writes results.json and prints a human-readable summary. No API keys needed.
